Subject: Observability partner surge-mode runbook: Datadog / Grafana / OpenTelemetry coordination

Team / partners —

We're kicking off runbook preparation for an expected ingestion surge tied to the Nimbus Analytics onboarding (Q1 pilot). Customer profile: heavy trace and span volume (~200k RPS of spans peak across multiple regions), short retention for raw traces but long retention for aggregates and embeddings. We need a coordinated partner playbook that covers:

- Ingestion hardening (OTLP relay recommendations, batching, backoff, sampling points)
- Storage/retention tradeoffs (indexes, TTLs, tiering guidance to control cost)
- Alerting & SLOs for ingest-backpressure and queue growth
- Emergency throttles and safe-fallback model variants
- Escalation contacts and on-call handoff matrix
- A simple test plan and checklist we can run during a staged ramp

I've attached a lightweight surge_runbook_template_v0.1.pdf and a couple of OTLP config snippets to seed the doc. Ask: can Datadog and Grafana each provide their playbook sections (1–2 pages each) plus any sample dashboards/queries we can import? Also please include recommended rate-limiting policies and sample relays/connectors we recommend for OTLP ingestion at scale.

Timeline: we'd like the first draft by EOD 2026-12-09 so we can schedule a joint 60-min workshop week of 12/13 to walk the plan and run the test checklist.

Thanks —
Mina Haddad
Partner Technical Program Manager | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Observability partner surge-mode runbook: Datadog / Grafana / OpenTelemetry coordination

Mina — thanks for the clear ask. Quick notes from the Datadog side (happy to expand into the 1–2 page playbook):

- Ingestion pipeline: recommend an OTLP relay (collector) in front of our intake with batching settings: max_batch_size=8192, max_latency_ms=200. Where possible use persistent connections and gRPC.
- Sampling: prefer tail-based sampling at the SDK/collector with a presampled subset forwarded for full-fidelity storage; apply attribute-based sampling to keep spans with error=true or latency>p95.
- Rate limiting: set soft-limits at 80% of observed peak with circuit-breaker thresholds to kick in at 95%. We'll provide a sample rate-policy that can be applied at the relay.
- Retention & storage: for traces we suggest short raw retention (7 days) with aggregated metrics/indices retained longer (90 days for metrics, 365 days for aggregates in cold storage). If Nimbus requires longer trace retention, recommend archive-to-object-store workflow.
- Alerts & SLOs: instrument queue length, OTLP receiver error rates, and persistent headroom. We'll propose thresholds and PagerDuty escalation steps.
- Test/validation: we can provide a k6 load profile and a small synthetic generator to emulate spike patterns.

Attachments I'll share after internal sign-off: datadog-surge-playbook-draft.pdf and datadog-rate-guidance.pdf.

Happy to join the workshop week of 12/13 — propose Thu 12/16 10:00 PT if that works.

Thanks Mina — adding Grafana-specific guidance below. Samir (cc) from Observability Consult will help us synthesize the joint runbook.

- Dashboards & visualizations: we will produce a starter dashboard JSON that covers ingest, latency percentiles, dropped spans, and a breakdown by region/service. That dashboard can be imported into Grafana Cloud and shared as a link.
- Logs/metrics backend: recommend using Loki for logs with index rotation configured to roll daily for high-volume sources. Retention policy suggestion: 14-days raw logs, then compress to long-term storage.
- Traces (Tempo): configure write buffers and the chunk target size tuned for short-lived bursts; recommend chunk_target_size=1MB for high throughput clients.
- OTLP: use the OpenTelemetry Collector as relay with the batch processor tuned to 500ms / 2000 spans per batch as a starting point. Provide connector examples for otlp_exporter -> tempo / loki / prometheus exporters.
- Limits: Grafana Cloud has ingestion limits per org — we'll provide a per-tenant plan and a temporary uplift option (surge capacity) for the Nimbus pilot window.

We can draft the Grafana section (including a dashboard JSON link and recommended Loki/Tempo config) and push it by 12/09. Week of 12/13 workshop is good; we prefer Thu 12/16 11:00 PT to avoid overlap with other commitments.
